Also carbon at 43.30 ppm (likely O-CH2). 26.29 ppm (likely CH3 of acetyl). Aromatic carbons: 132.43,130.27,129.30,126.70,126.66,123.57 (six aromatic carbons). So benzene ring with two substituents (disubstituted). The pattern of aromatic protons: 4 protons, likely para-disubstituted (AA'BB') would give two doublets, not ddd. Or ortho-disubstituted gives complex pattern of 4 protons (two doublets of doublets). The given pattern ddd suggests maybe 1,2,4-trisubstituted? That would have 3 aromatic protons. But we have 4. Could be 1,2-disubstituted (ortho) gives 4 protons with complex splitting. So likely ortho-disubstituted benzene.
